David / Jordan —

Quick status: I pulled the compact inventory and focused the CSV on production-facing processors over the last 90 days. Columns included: vendor_name, service_name, processor_role (telemetry/storage/relay/kms), primary_country, has_kms (yes/no), egress_jurisdictions, and retention_window_days. I redacted internal hostnames and tenant IDs to keep it compact. See attached: redwood_subprocessors_compact.csv.

Also attaching the prod shadowing runbook (prod-shadowing-steps.pdf). Highlights for Apex:
- Shadowing is executed with a time-limited, read-only telemetry stream; no writes to their buckets are permitted.
- KV cache/prefix caching is isolated per-customer; we run canary routing to onshore fallback when subtended relays are in maintenance.
- Escrow/attestation: we have an HSM/KMS jurisdiction map and can provide a limited attestation (not full escrow) within a DPA addendum.

On the DPA addendum: if Apex asks for "escrow" for a temporary processor, legal will likely want a scoped addendum rather than a blanket escrow. I drafted a short addendum template and attached as dpa-addendum-draft.docx — it's targeted at temporary telemetry/relay partners only.

Notes on blockers: two small telemetry relays show "transit through EU" for a small percentage of events (less than 0.5%). If Apex requires strict US-only residency for all processing, we should surface that as an exception early.

I can package this and send to Elena with a one-paragraph executive summary.

—Kimberly Park
Privacy & Compliance Manager, Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood_subprocessors_compact.csv; prod-shadowing-steps.pdf; dpa-addendum-draft.docx
